name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_UNIT6_Q01 - Ores versus minerals and hydraulic washing

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: All ores are minerals, but all minerals cannot be used as ores for the extraction of a metal.

Statement II: Hydraulic washing is a gravity separation method based on the difference between specific gravities of the ore and the gangue particles.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Naturally occurring chemical substances obtained by mining are minerals, whereas concentration methods separate desired ore particles from earthly gangue.

Step 2: Evaluation of the Claims
Among the many minerals in which a metal may occur, only those from which extraction is chemically feasible and commercially viable are classified as ores; hence, every ore is a mineral, but not every mineral is an ore. Furthermore, hydraulic washing uses an upward stream of running water to wash away lighter gangue particles while leaving heavier ore particles behind, making it a gravity separation method based on differences in specific gravity.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Both statements are correct.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_UNIT6_Q02 - Leaching of bauxite and cyanide leaching of gold

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: During the leaching of bauxite with concentrated \(\mathrm{NaOH}\) at \(473\text{--}523\,\mathrm{K}\), \(\mathrm{Al_2O_3}\) dissolves as sodium aluminate and \(\mathrm{SiO_2}\) dissolves as sodium silicate.

Statement II: In the cyanide leaching of gold, zinc acts as an oxidising agent to convert metallic gold into \([\mathrm{Au(CN)_2}]^-\).

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Leaching selectively dissolves the target metal or oxide in a suitable solvent, and in gold metallurgy, recovery from the cyanide complex occurs via reductive displacement.

Step 2: Evaluation of the Claims
When powdered bauxite is heated with concentrated \(\mathrm{NaOH}\) at \(473\text{--}523\,\mathrm{K}\) and \(35\text{--}36\,\mathrm{bar}\), \(\mathrm{Al_2O_3}\) is extracted as sodium aluminate (\(\mathrm{NaAl(OH)_4}\)) and the \(\mathrm{SiO_2}\) impurity also dissolves as sodium silicate, leaving iron oxides and \(\mathrm{TiO_2}\) behind; thus the first claim is correct. In gold extraction, atmospheric \(\mathrm{O_2}\) oxidises metallic gold to \([\mathrm{Au(CN)_2}]^-\), whereas zinc is added later as a reducing agent to displace and precipitate metallic gold while forming \([\mathrm{Zn(CN)_4}]^{2-}\); thus the second claim is incorrect.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The first claim is correct, whereas the second claim is incorrect.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_UNIT6_Q03 - Calcination versus roasting and copper matte

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Calcination is carried out by heating sulphide ores in a regular supply of air to convert them into metal oxides and \(\mathrm{SO_2}\).

Statement II: During copper smelting in a reverberatory furnace, silica combines with \(\mathrm{FeO}\) to form \(\mathrm{FeSiO_3}\) slag while copper is obtained as copper matte containing \(\mathrm{Cu_2S}\) and \(\mathrm{FeS}\).

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Calcination and roasting are distinct thermal pretreatment processes, and smelting of iron-bearing copper sulphide ores uses silica as a flux.

Step 2: Evaluation of the Claims
Heating sulphide ores in a regular supply of air below the melting point of the metal to form metal oxides and \(\mathrm{SO_2}\) is roasting, not calcination (calcination removes volatile matter such as water or \(\mathrm{CO_2}\) from hydrated oxides or carbonates); therefore, the first claim is incorrect. In a reverberatory furnace, silica reacts with \(\mathrm{FeO}\) to form \(\mathrm{FeSiO_3}\) slag while copper is produced as copper matte containing \(\mathrm{Cu_2S}\) and \(\mathrm{FeS}\); therefore, the second claim is correct.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The first claim is incorrect, whereas the second claim is correct.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_UNIT6_Q04 - Properties of pig iron and wrought iron

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Pig iron obtained from the blast furnace contains about \(0.15\%\) carbon and is the purest form of commercial iron.

Statement II: Wrought iron is made by melting pig iron with scrap iron and coke using a hot air blast, and is extremely hard and brittle.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Pig iron, cast iron, and wrought iron differ in their carbon content, purity, and mechanical properties.

Step 2: Evaluation of the Claims
Pig iron obtained from the blast furnace contains about \(4\%\) carbon along with impurities like \(\mathrm{S}\), \(\mathrm{P}\), \(\mathrm{Si}\), and \(\mathrm{Mn}\), so it is not the purest form of commercial iron; thus the first claim is incorrect. Melting pig iron with scrap iron and coke using a hot air blast produces cast iron (about \(3\%\) carbon), which is extremely hard and brittle, whereas wrought iron is malleable and is the purest form of commercial iron prepared in a haematite-lined reverberatory furnace; thus the second claim is also incorrect.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Both statements are incorrect.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_UNIT6_Q05 - Electrolytic refining of copper and van Arkel method

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In the electrolytic refining of copper, impure copper is made the anode and pure copper strips are taken as the cathode in an acidified \(\mathrm{CuSO_4}\) electrolyte.

Statement II: In the van Arkel method for refining zirconium, crude \(\mathrm{Zr}\) is heated with iodine to form volatile \(\mathrm{ZrI_4}\), which is decomposed on a tungsten filament heated to about \(1800\,\mathrm{K}\).

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Metals can be refined to high purity by electrochemical transfer (electrolytic refining) or by forming and decomposing volatile compounds (vapour phase refining).

Step 2: Evaluation of the Claims
In electrolytic refining of copper, impure copper serves as the anode, pure copper strips serve as the cathode, and acidified \(\mathrm{CuSO_4}\) solution serves as the electrolyte, transferring pure copper from anode to cathode. In the van Arkel method for zirconium, crude \(\mathrm{Zr}\) reacts with \(\mathrm{I_2}\) in an evacuated vessel to form covalent volatile \(\mathrm{ZrI_4}\), which decomposes on an electrically heated tungsten filament at about \(1800\,\mathrm{K}\) to deposit pure \(\mathrm{Zr}\).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Both statements are correct.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_UNIT6_Q06 - Ellingham diagram slopes and ZnO reduction

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: For the reaction \(2\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{s}) + \mathrm{O_2}(\mathrm{g}) \rightarrow 2\mathrm{CO}(\mathrm{g})\), \(\Delta S\) is positive, so the \(\Delta_{\mathrm{r}}G^{\ominus}\) versus \(T\) curve slopes downwards with increasing temperature.

Statement II: In the Ellingham diagram, the \(\mathrm{CO, CO_2}\) line lies below the \(\mathrm{Zn, ZnO}\) line, which is why \(\mathrm{ZnO}\) is commercially reduced using \(\mathrm{CO}\) rather than coke.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The slope of a line in an Ellingham diagram is \(-\Delta S\), and a reducing agent can reduce a metal oxide only if its oxidation line lies below the metal oxide formation line.

Step 2: Evaluation of the Claims
In \(2\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{s}) + \mathrm{O_2}(\mathrm{g}) \rightarrow 2\mathrm{CO}(\mathrm{g})\), \(1\,\mathrm{mol}\) of gas yields \(2\,\mathrm{mol}\) of gas, so \(\Delta S\) is positive and \(-T\Delta S\) is negative, giving a downward slope; thus the first claim is correct. However, in the Ellingham diagram, the \(\mathrm{CO, CO_2}\) line lies above the \(\mathrm{Zn, ZnO}\) line, so \(\mathrm{CO}\) cannot reduce \(\mathrm{ZnO}\); instead, coke is used to reduce \(\mathrm{ZnO}\) at \(1673\,\mathrm{K}\) because the \(\mathrm{C, CO}\) line drops below the \(\mathrm{Zn, ZnO}\) line at high temperatures; thus the second claim is incorrect.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The first claim is correct, whereas the second claim is incorrect.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_UNIT6_Q07 - Hall Heroult electrodes and brine electrolysis

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In the Hall-Heroult process for aluminium extraction, \(\mathrm{Al^{3+}}\) ions are reduced at the graphite anode while \(\mathrm{CO}\) and \(\mathrm{CO_2}\) are liberated at the carbon-lined cathode.

Statement II: Electrolysis of aqueous \(\mathrm{NaCl}\) yields metallic sodium at the cathode because \(\Delta G^{\ominus}\) for chlorine evolution from brine is negative.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
During electrolysis, cations are reduced at the cathode and anions are oxidised at the anode; in aqueous solutions, water can be preferentially reduced over highly reactive metal cations.

Step 2: Evaluation of the Claims
In the Hall-Heroult process, \(\mathrm{Al^{3+}}\) ions are reduced to molten aluminium at the carbon-lined steel cathode, while oxide ions are oxidised at the graphite anode to produce \(\mathrm{CO}\) and \(\mathrm{CO_2}\); thus the first claim is incorrect. In the electrolysis of aqueous \(\mathrm{NaCl}\) (brine), \(\Delta G^{\ominus}\) for \(2\mathrm{Cl^-} + 2\mathrm{H_2O} \rightarrow 2\mathrm{OH^-} + \mathrm{H_2} + \mathrm{Cl_2}\) is positive (\(+422\,\mathrm{kJ}\)), and the products are \(\mathrm{Cl_2}\), \(\mathrm{H_2}\), and aqueous \(\mathrm{NaOH}\)—metallic \(\mathrm{Na}\) is produced only from molten \(\mathrm{NaCl}\), not aqueous \(\mathrm{NaCl}\); thus the second claim is also incorrect.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Both statements are incorrect.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
